**No.** `CatalogApi.CreateItem` does not publish `ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent` — it publishes no integration events at all.

What `CreateItem` actually does (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:366-388`):
1. Takes `CatalogServices services` and a `CatalogItem product` from the request body (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:366-368`).
2. Constructs a new `CatalogItem` from the posted product, copying `Id`, `CatalogBrandId`, `CatalogTypeId`, `Description`, `PictureFileName`, `Price`, `AvailableStock`, `RestockThreshold`, and `MaxStockThreshold` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:370-381`).
3. Computes and assigns an AI embedding via `services.CatalogAI.GetEmbeddingAsync(item)` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:382`).
4. Adds the item to `services.Context.CatalogItems` and calls `SaveChangesAsync()` — a plain EF Core insert, with no `services.EventService` usage (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:384-385`).
5. Returns `TypedResults.Created($"/api/catalog/items/{item.Id}")` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:387`). It is registered as the `POST /items` endpoint named "CreateItem" (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:103-104`).

How I established this: `ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent` appears in `CatalogApi.cs` at exactly one place — line 350, inside `UpdateItem`, not `CreateItem`. There, when the EF `Price` property is flagged as modified, the event is created and published via `services.EventService.SaveEventAndCatalogContextChangesAsync` and `PublishThroughEventBusAsync` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:345-357`). `CreateItem`'s body (lines 366-388) contains no reference to `EventService` or any integration event.

One nuance worth flagging: `UpdateOrCreateItem` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:315-322`) delegates to `UpdateItem`, not to `CreateItem`, so the event-publishing path is reached only through the update flow.
